elaine: FYI onboarding trial for atlas-13b-int8-q shows a repeatable long-context mismatch tied to RoPE phase clipping around token ~11,200 when using our delta-KV snapshot flow.

elaine: experiment details: model=atlas-13b:int8, prime files=tests/11k_techdoc_mix.txt, prime_len=11200, gen_len=600, snapshots every 1400 tokens, compare against fp16 baseline.

omar: is it an obvious off-by-one in KV index or attenuation?

elaine: initial traces point to phase wrapping changing energy contribution for tokens at distance >8192. The int8 packed pathway emits slightly lower magnitude for V vectors on later layers.

jin: can you share the reproduction command and the key log lines?

elaine: repro:
```
MODEL=atlas-13b:int8
python run_long_onboard.py \
  --model $MODEL \
  --prompt tests/11k_techdoc_mix.txt \
  --prime-len 11200 \
  --gen-len 600 \
  --kv-snapshots true \
  --snap-interval 1400 \
  --seed 101
```
logs snippet:
```
[DEBUG] layer=20 token=11200 k_norm=0.987 v_norm=0.812
[DEBUG] layer=20 token=11201 k_norm=0.986 v_norm=0.793  # int8 path
[WARN] kvcache: phase_clip_threshold_exceeded layer=20 token=11202
```

omar: v_norm drop of ~2% could shift attention distribution enough to flip a punctuation token over many steps.

jin: did you check snapshot integrity across quantized vs fp16? checksums or shapes mismatch?

elaine: shapes match. checksums diverge starting at snapshot 8 (snapshot indexes start at 0). Snapshot 7 matches within tolerance, snapshot 8 shows per-layer V max-abs ~1e-3 difference on layers 18-22.

omar: that region aligns with where RoPE scaling starts to wrap for our implementation. Maybe quant rounding interacts with the rotary basis extrapolation for large positions.

elaine: plan: 1) run int8 with --rotary-clamp=off to test if clamp is amplifying rounding, 2) run int8 with higher quant bits for KV (int8->int16 sim) to see sensitivity, 3) add a debug dump of per-layer RoPE cos/sin values at snapshot boundaries.

jin: add also a KV-replay test: load snapshots into a fresh fp16 runtime and compare generation step-by-step; that isolates whether snapshots are the source vs inference-time kernel differences. I can adapt replay_snapshots.py.

ci-bot: build passed on branch "ropex-int8-probe"; artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/ropex-int8-probe/1751119999

elaine: quick early results: disabling rotary clamp removed the phase_clip warnings but outputs still diverged slightly by token 11250. Running int16-sim for KV reduces delta significantly.

omar: that suggests quantization granularity in KV values is a key multiplier. If int16-sim stabilizes, we might add a mixed-precision rule: keep KV as int16-like when prime_len > X.

jin: agree, but that's a policy change. For now we need a mitigation: recommend a snapshot write guard that records per-layer V quant_scale and a checksum of raw float pre-quantize values so we can correlate deltas later.

elaine: logging guard added locally. Also uploading a small sample of diffs to s3://redwood-debug/ropex-11200-1751119999/; will post CSVs for per-layer max-abs and cosine-phase cross-corr.

omar: thanks. After we have the replay results, let's do a narrow bisect on the quant packer commit range and the RoPE clamp changes. Could be an interaction.

elaine: assigned: jin -> replay tool and per-step compare, omar -> quant packer bisect, elaine -> telemetry and guard metrics. Will update thread when artifacts complete.

ci-bot: longctx matrix job started: run-id 2026-03-21-1905.

elaine: early verdict: int16-sim KV is strong signal. Moving to draft a canary policy that pins KV to higher precision for contexts exceeding 10k tokens while we investigate. Tagging @eng-ml for awareness.

jin: uploading compare CSVs in 20m.

elaine: thanks — keeping this as single-threaded triage for this issue.
